messages:
carmen: Quick follow-up from the RFC — we need a minimal, explicit contract between the Queue and Scheduler before starting the refactor.
ben: +1, please paste the sketch so we avoid assumptions that tripped us last sprint.
carmen: Core principles: (1) queue holds requests + lightweight routing metadata only; (2) scheduler owns admission, quotas, preempt decisions; (3) scheduler -> queue uses typed signals (not booleans). Minimal proto sketch below.
```
interface WorkQueue {
  Enqueue(req)
  Dequeue(maxTokens) -> [req]
  UpdatePressure(state, reason, details) // state: idle|throttle|reject, reason short enum, details freeform
  MarkPreempt(selector, mode) // mode: soft-handoff|hard-eject
  ReturnHandoffToken(token_str)
  EmitEvent(name, tags, value)
}

interface Scheduler {
  Admit(req) -> {decision: admit|buffer|preempt, handoff_token?: string}
  ReleaseCredits(n)
  RequestEviction(selector)
}
```
alex: I like typed MarkPreempt instead of ad-hoc flags.
priya: Durable quota state should live in scheduler. Queue may keep a tiny LRU cache for fast local rejects (eventual consistency only).
ben: +1 — queue cache must never be the source of truth.
mike: Handoff token must be compact and idempotent. Example wire-format: "handoff:tid=12345;ofs=512;count=8;v=1;cs=abcd" (version + checksum).
priya: Allow partial minibatch returns but require idempotency_id + offset to avoid KV re-apply.
carmen: Telemetry hooks: queue should emit events enqueued, dequeued, preempt_mark, handoff_issued, pressure_update. Tag with tenant, model, seq_len_bucket. Surface metrics preempt_latency_ms and handoff_size_bytes.
alex: Safety knobs: headroom cap per-machine and per-tenant (config: max_borrow_pct). Default 20%.
priya: Tradeoff: soft-handoff reduces hard ejects but can increase victims' tail p99. Gate enablement behind console flag and surface per-tenant p95/p99 before enabling.
mike: Preemption flow (2-step): Scheduler.RequestEviction(selector) -> Queue.MarkPreempt(selector, soft-handoff) -> queue stops coalescing for affected slots and issues small handoff token(s) -> scheduler drains or migrates. For hard-eject, queue returns ditch list immediately and cancels coalescing.
ben: UpdatePressure should include a reason enum: kernel_saturation|mem_pressure|pack_delay to help ops triage.
carmen: Migration plan: (1) implement a thin shim that exports WorkQueue over the current queue impl, (2) dogfood internally on a low-risk tenant, (3) enable canary 5% with flag scheduler.v2.queue_contract=true, (4) monitor preempt_latency_ms, handoff_rate, tenant_p95, burst_drop_rate, (5) roll by config.
infra-bot: created canary job INF-827-canary (queued).
ben: I'll add dashboards & alerts: preempt_latency > 200ms, handoff_rate spikes, cache_reject_rate > 1%.
alex: API nit: UpdatePressure(name) -> UpdatePressure(state, reason, details) is better so we carry short diagnostic details (max 256 chars).
priya: Handoff caps: keep handoff tokens < 64KB and < 50ms to generate; otherwise prefer draining to avoid long stalls. Also keep handoff token idempotent.
mike: Tests: e2e with two tenants and induced mem_pressure; assert soft-handoff cuts hard_ejects and no KV corruption. Add property tests for idempotent ReturnHandoffToken semantics.
carmen: Timeline: prototype shim this week, e2e tests next week, canary by end of sprint if green. I'll write a short follow-up doc with token wire-format and example traces.
ben: Tracking in INF-827. Thanks all :thumbsup:
